query: What factors explain low review scores?

per_column.name: product_category
per_column.rationale: Product category plausibly affects both the type/likelihood of complaints (treatments like brew strength, palatability) and the baseline review score, since some categories systematically attract lower ratings. It is a genuine common cause surfaced from the data, not named in the query.

per_column.name: brew_strength_complaint
per_column.rationale: A brew-strength complaint is an expressed dissatisfaction extracted from the review text; it lies on the causal path to giving a low score (it is essentially a reason the reviewer scored low), so it mediates rather than confounds the outcome.

per_column.name: palatability_rejection
per_column.rationale: Refusal/rejection of the product on taste grounds is an intermediate reaction that leads to a low score; it is on the causal path, so it is a mediator, not a common cause.

per_column.name: product_freshness_staleness
per_column.rationale: Whether the product was stale is a candidate observed cause whose effect on the low score is being attributed; it is a plausible treatment/cause of the outcome.

per_column.name: product_performance_failure
per_column.rationale: A product failing to perform (no effect/adverse effect) is a candidate cause of the low score being attributed; treatable as a treatment/cause variable.

per_column.name: fulfillment_service_failure
per_column.rationale: A shipping/fulfillment failure is a candidate observed cause of a low score, distinct from product quality; it is a plausible treatment.

per_column.name: ingredient_transparency_concern
per_column.rationale: Concern about ingredient transparency is a candidate cause of dissatisfaction and low scores; a plausible treatment/cause.

judge.rationale: The added columns supply multiple candidate causes (treatments) extracted from the review text, so requirement (a) is met. However, the causal-estimation setup is weak on requirement (b): almost all columns are themselves candidate causes/reasons for the low score rather than common causes of both a treatment and the outcome. Several (brew_strength_complaint, palatability_rejection) are mediators — expressed dissatisfaction on the path to the score — and labelling them confounders would be an error. The only plausible genuine confounder is product_category, which can drive both which complaints arise and baseline scores, and it was surfaced from the data (not named in the query). But it is a single, coarse confounder and no reviewer/context common causes (e.g., reviewer strictness, price paid, expectation) were adjusted for. So there is limited real confounder reasoning, yielding modest confounder quality.
